output.methodChoice: EDF analysis, collected X3 and X13 (2 of 2 items)
output.brief: The yield drop is mainly a scholarship effect, not a portal effect. Dean's and Merit tier yields fell about 13 points each (45% to 32%), while Presidential and no-award tiers barely moved. The October 2025 schedule cut Dean's awards from $14,000 to $9,000 and Merit from $9,000 to $5,000. Early action, decided on the legacy system on time, fell as much as regular decision (45% to 38% versus 39% to 31.5%), so the slow portal turnaround does not explain most of the loss. Applications and admits rose, so a smaller pool is not the cause. I am moderately confident; the link is not proven by a controlled comparison, and the merit-review staffing effect is untested. Next: have finance model restoring the Dean's and Merit award levels before next cycle's letters go out. Separately, do not replace the director on this evidence. Confirm the missing-transcript issue by checking the file records directly, and measure yield by segment.
